_note: Every row states what is already known (with its source), what is missing, how to find it, who can answer, and whether a decision is blocked without it.
Rows marked 'answered this cycle' or 'answered in repo' carry an answer and, where one exists, the source that settles it. check.py fails the build if an
open question carries an answer, or if an answered question cites a source that was not actually opened - so the register cannot quietly fill itself in.

questions.question: When does the official Week 10 report become decision-grade, and how much does it move between capture and kickoff?
questions.known: Three official pages for one week disagree about one player (desk/reconcile.html N01) and the Friday roundup contains rulings-out that the article had as questionable. The report page read on 2026-11-13 shows game statuses for Sunday's slate and blanks for rows the policy says are 'certain to play'.
questions.unknown: The publication schedule for each day's report, the deadline after which a designation cannot change, and where the final inactive list is published officially.
questions.how_to_discover: Snapshot the same club-week on Wednesday, Thursday and Friday for four consecutive weeks and diff. If the league publishes a deadline statement anywhere, find it and cite it; the injury-report policy article retrieved this cycle (A06) does not state one.
questions.who_can_answer: NFL.com / club PR; an owner decision on tolerable staleness is the other half.

questions.question: What does a blank Game Status mean: 'not yet published', 'not applicable', or 'certain to play'?
questions.known: The official policy wording retrieved this cycle states that a player certain to play is no longer listed in the club's Game Status Report, that Probable was eliminated, and that a such a player who is then deactivated requires an explanation to the league. Applied to the captured data, this is the only reading that makes the LAC and BAL rows coherent (17 and 8 rows, all with a blank status, on the eve of a Monday game).
questions.unknown: Whether that wording is the rule in force in 2026: the retrieved page carries no date and no 'in force from' statement (flag F02).
questions.how_to_discover: Find a dated policy document (Game Operations Manual, bylaws amendment, or a league memo) or a newer Competition Committee article. Until then, treat 'certain to play' as a labelled interpretation, not as a fact.
questions.who_can_answer: NFL league operations; the owner decides the evidence bar (K03).
questions.answer: The blank is meaningful, not missing: under the published revision, a player certain to play is removed from the Game Status Report, so an empty cell alongside a DNP or limited practice entry is an availability statement. This desk publishes the interpretation with its caveat and does not impute a designation.

questions.question: What is a stable key for a player across the report, the article, the roundup and the roster?
questions.known: This cycle's answer is worse than the previous one: one Arizona designation is published under three different player URLs - /players/zach-carter (article), /players/zachary-carter (roundup) and /players/zachary-carter-x9168 (report, with position DT while the other two say DL). Name matching would join none of them cleanly.
questions.unknown: Whether the numeric league athlete ID appears in a retrievable official page for every player, and whether it is stable across the three page types.
questions.how_to_discover: Open a player's official profile page (A07-style) and record whatever numeric identifier the URL or page carries; test whether the three page types expose it. A handful of reads answers this; it has never been answered here.
questions.who_can_answer: Engineering answer from the pages themselves; the owner decides whether to key on it.

questions.question: Where can first, second, third and fourth string depth ordering be obtained from an official publisher?
questions.known: Re-probed today: nfl.com/depth-charts/ is 404 (A08); a legacy static JSON path returns 500 (A10); the league's club roster page carries membership and a status code but no ordering per a prior session's record (A09). Club-published pages exist and resolve (C01 proves the club sites are live) but this session did not open a club depth-chart page, so club-level ordering is recorded as unverified, not as impossible.
questions.unknown: Whether each of the 32 club sites publishes a dated depth chart, how often it updates, and whether the repository will accept club domains as official.
questions.how_to_discover: Open depth-chart pages on the 28 clubs in this slate, record URL, last-updated statement and whether a string column is present. One cycle of fetches. If it is present, the requirement becomes sourceable; if not, K04/K05 decide the fallback.
questions.who_can_answer: The clubs publish it; the owner decides the tier.

questions.question: Why were DEN, CHI, PHI and TB absent from the previous cycle's Week 10 capture?
questions.known: Answered this cycle: the official Week 10 scores page lists them under 'Teams on Bye' with records CHI 7-2, DEN 7-2, PHI 2-7, TB 3-6, and the statuses article states the slate is 14 games (14x2+4=32). The previous capture's 'not known whether on bye' is now closed.
questions.unknown: Nothing about this week. The general question - whether absence in the report always equals bye - becomes a gate rather than an inference (K02).
questions.how_to_discover: Read the bye list on the same scores page each cycle; do not infer it from an empty club.
questions.answer: Bye. Confirmed from the official scores page rather than inferred, and recorded as flag F01 so the earlier reasoning is visible as corrected.

questions.question: Should 'no designations printed for this club' be treated as an error rather than as data?
questions.known: The article promises statuses for all 14 games and prints none for the Monday clubs (flag F04). A parser that reads absence as zero absences is silently wrong once a week, every Monday-night week.
questions.unknown: How often this happens - byes, Monday games, and any week where one club files late.
questions.how_to_discover: Run the article parser over four weeks and count club-weeks with no list. No new source needed; the pages are addressable by week.
questions.who_can_answer: Engineering; then the owner sets the fail-open/fail-closed rule.

questions.question: What is the complete vocabulary of official roster status codes, and how do roster status, practice status and game status interact?
questions.known: This cycle's pages show at least five vocabularies in use: ACT (roster), injured reserve, PUP, and the three practice statuses, with game status separate. Two Packers/Dolphins designations coexist with an IR mention in the prose (N06, N15), which means IR is not a synonym for unavailable at the game level - or the prose is loose.
questions.unknown: The definitions and the eligibility rule for a player designated while on IR, plus the full code list.
questions.how_to_discover: The league's roster-status rules and the CBA/injury-settlement language; the club roster page is the only table this session has seen that carries a status column at all.
questions.who_can_answer: NFL operations / the CBA; not retrievable from the pages opened so far.

questions.question: Against what benchmark is an originated line judged, given that no official publisher releases prices?
questions.known: The repository has one answer and it is a third-party, pinned, hashed dataset (nflverse/nfldata at a270278f), whose five files this desk re-hashed today at 5/5 identical. Every accuracy, ROI, CLV and gate figure in this repository is measured against that file, and README's own headline (10.670 vs 10.247 MAE) is reproduced by the published sensitivity grid.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner will licence a real price feed, accept the pinned dataset indefinitely with its own terms, or restrict the system to non-market outputs (accuracy against final scores, which the league does publish).
questions.how_to_discover: A decision plus, if licensing is chosen, a terms review; there is nothing to fetch that settles it.

questions.question: What price does the model assume it gets, and can that assumption be tested?
questions.known: The published protocol bounds prices to -125..+400 and requires a 3% edge, the ledgers disclose 26.9% of prices imputed at -110, and gate P07 asks whether a result survives at -115. There is no execution model and no fill data.
questions.unknown: Slippage, limit-vs-market, and whether the imputed-price share is large enough to flip any result (the pipeline publishes roi_minus115 per row for exactly this reason).
questions.how_to_discover: A paper-fill log against a single operator, or an owner decision to treat fills as unknown and keep the stress test as the bar.
questions.who_can_answer: Owner; an operator's public rules page can supply the settlement vocabulary but not the fills.

questions.question: Which settlement rules apply to a leg inside a parlay when it pushes, voids or is cancelled, and who publishes them authoritatively?
questions.known: The dependence requirement is measurable and is published here: the 2-leg breakeven phi at -110 is 0.0975, measured same-game spread x total phi is +0.0161 and spread x home-ML is +0.6706, all recomputed from the ledger's own marginals. That is the arithmetic half.
questions.unknown: The rules half: which operator terms govern a void leg, and whether official player-prop lines exist anywhere in machine-readable form (they do not, per this repository's backlog B01 and the props block in the summary artifact).
questions.how_to_discover: Operator terms pages for the venues the owner would actually use, and one pass over the league's stats endpoints to see whether any prop-level official line exists.
questions.who_can_answer: Operators publish; the owner decides which terms are in scope.

questions.question: What sample size separates a strategy from luck, and does the repository already pay that price?
questions.known: Published nulls say no: with 2,000 simulations of 11 random strategies, best-of-family ROI averages +5.45% (5th-95th -0.35% to +16.28%) and the best of eleven is profitable 93.05% of the time. The desk's own power arithmetic puts a 2-point win-rate edge at about 4,900 bets for 80% power and 6,500 for 90%, against a best observed n of 607.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner accepts gates that no current strategy passes - i.e. whether the competition is allowed to have no winner this season.
questions.how_to_discover: Nothing to fetch. It is a policy decision with a stated cost: honest gates mean an empty leaderboard.

questions.question: What can lawfully be offered as a reward, by whom, and is any pool funded?
questions.known: Nothing is funded: the docs leaderboard records reward_units 0.0 across all 15 rows, the verified workbench records reward null with status not_eligible, and no ledger marks any strategy eligible.
questions.unknown: Jurisdiction and licensing, and whether the reward should be monetary at all.
questions.how_to_discover: A legal review the owner must commission; this repository should not propose an amount.

questions.question: Do member-club domains count as official publishers repository-wide?
questions.known: This desk treats them as a separate tier and cites one (C01) for a schedule fact only. decision_lab admits one club domain inside its own directory and records the wider question as unanswered; the repository-wide allow-list in verify/source_audit.py does not include club domains.
questions.how_to_discover: A decision, then one line in the shared allow-list plus a re-run of the audit - which is an integration change, not a desk change.

questions.question: Can a reader reproduce this desk from its data, and can a reader verify the capture from the links?
questions.known: Yes to reproduction: desk/build.py and desk/build_ledger.py are deterministic, and desk/check.py re-runs the ledger derivation and fails on drift. Partly to verification: every designation row links the page it was transcribed from, but 159 of 160 rows were not individually re-opened (one was, A07).
questions.unknown: How much verification depth the owner wants per cycle (K13 option A costs about 160 page reads).
questions.how_to_discover: Decide, then automate; the check already separates 'linked' from 're-opened'.
questions.who_can_answer: Owner for the budget; this directory for the implementation.
questions.answer: Rebuild and re-check are reproducible today: run python3 desk/build.py, python3 desk/build_ledger.py and python3 desk/check.py and the output must be byte-identical with 0 failures. Row-level re-verification is sampled, and the sample rate is published rather than implied.

questions.question: Can the capture run without a human, given that this sandbox cannot reach nfl.com from the shell?
questions.known: This session read every page through a fetching tool at session time; a repository-side job would need an egress path, a parser and a schedule. Nothing in the repo currently refreshes injury data on its own, and the brief rules out manual input from the owner.
questions.unknown: Whether a scheduled fetch is permitted from the owner's infrastructure, and what the terms of use permit for storage versus redistribution.
questions.how_to_discover: One controlled experiment: a scheduled job that stores a page-text hash per club-week and nothing else, then a terms review of what may be retained.

questions.question: Which surface is the front door, and what happens to the other nine?
questions.known: Unchanged and still the cheapest open item to close: 11 index pages exist and this desk adds a twelfth path; the root nav is generated, so an added entry survives only if it is added to the generator.

questions.question: Which signal families are still untried, as opposed to tried and failed?
questions.known: From the consolidated ledger: own-line-vs-close edges, Elo margin, wind/unders, short week, bye, divisional home dog, rest differential and scoring-profile totals have all been tested and none is eligible. Not tested, because the input does not exist in the repository: practice-status changes as an event (KQ01), transaction-driven availability (F10), and any positional-replacement feature (F03).
questions.unknown: Whether the three untested families are testable at all before K04/K07/K11 are decided - the second is, the third is not without a depth decision.
questions.how_to_discover: Two weeks of captures answer it for family 2 without any new licence. Family 3 waits on K04/K05.

questions.question: What is the system for, and where is the line between modelling a market and advising a bet?
questions.known: Every surface in this repository, including this one, states that no strategy has cleared its gates and that nothing here is betting advice. The gates are close to unpassable by design, and the honest reading of this cycle is that the system is a research instrument, not a source of picks.
questions.unknown: Whether the owner wants the reward competition to publish anything at all while the answer to KQ11 is 'no winner yet'.
